To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the centrality dependence for the average multiplicity of identified particles is well described by the core-corona picture, that the centrality dependent elliptic flow is well reproduced in this model, that the single particle spectra of all charged and identified particle species can be explained by the core-corrona picture, and that the average momentum of particles with similar masses can be quite different and therefore cannot be used as a measure of a collective expansion.

the centrality dependence for the production of protons, kaons, $K^-$ mesons and antiprotons in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}$ = 200GeV at RHIC are well described by a core-corona model with two free parameters, the fraction of the produced particles which belong to the corona and the average momentum of the particles in the corona.
the core-corona picture of the reaction zone in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC energies is confirmed by the data of all three collaborations.
